records.title: September jobs numbers weaker than expected
records.quote: Economists had expected September payrolls to come in around 90,000
records.about: The Associated Press dispatch by Paul Wiseman, saved after the release. PBS NewsHour carries the same dispatch.

records.title: Disappointing 29,000 jobs added in September
records.quote: Hiring dropped from a revised 133,000 in August, the Labor Department reported
records.about: PBS NewsHour's page of the Associated Press dispatch, bylined Paul Wiseman.

records.title: September jobs report shows slowdown in hiring, rise in unemployment
records.quote: The Labor Department estimates U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September
records.about: USA Today's account of the release.

records.title: Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, short of forecasts
records.quote: Economists had forecast the economy would add 90,000 new jobs last month, according to financial data firm FactSet
records.about: CBS News, including the FactSet forecast of 90,000.

records.title: Labor market faltered in September
records.quote: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had been looking for job growth of 84,000 and an unemployment rate of 4.1%
records.about: CNBC's account, including the Dow Jones survey and a workweek figure the release does not support.

records.title: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September
records.quote: employers added just 29,000 jobs last month
records.about: NPR's account of the same release.

records.title: U.S. added 29,000 jobs in September; unemployment up to 4.2%
records.quote: the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%
records.about: UPI's account of the release.

records.title: US economy added 29,000 jobs in September
records.quote: The unemployment rate also ticked up slightly to 4.2 percent
records.about: The Hill's account of the release.

records.title: What to expect from the September jobs report
records.quote: Wall Street is looking for job growth of 84,000
records.about: CNBC's preview the day before the release, citing a Dow Jones consensus of 84,000 jobs and a 4.1 percent rate.

records.title: U.S. job growth expected to slow in September
records.quote: Nonfarm payrolls likely increased by 90,000 last month
records.about: Reuters' preview, published before 8:30 a.m. Eastern, with a survey of 90,000 jobs and a 4.1 percent rate.

records.title: Jobs report could show hiring stayed resilient in September
records.quote: Economists expect U.S. employers to have added 84,000 jobs in September
records.about: ABC News' preview, expecting 84,000 jobs. Written before the release.

records.title: Flash Report: Unemployment Rises Slightly, Job Growth Slows in September
records.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
records.quote: More precise data show the rate increased slightly from 4.141% to 4.175%.
records.about: The unrounded unemployment rate, 4.141 percent in August and 4.175 percent in September.

records.title: US job growth undershoots expectations in September, but labor market remains stable
records.quote: Economists estimated that the economy needs to create roughly 50,000 jobs per month to keep up with growth in the working-age population.
records.about: Reuters's post-release story: the 50,000 working-age yardstick, a late Labor Day as one account of a weak September, the government-payroll split, and the October 27-28 rate-hike odds.

records.title: Press Briefing: Kevin Hassett Speaks to Reporters Outside the White House
records.quote: What's happened is because we've reduced federal employment by 300,000 workers, then the numbers, uh, are a little bit lower if you don't account for that.
records.about: Kevin Hassett's October 2 briefing outside the White House, in the Factbase transcript. The page template is dated April 22, 2024; the transcript heading is October 2, 2026.

records.title: Kevin Hassett says jobs numbers have been blockbuster
records.quote: Kevin Hassett, the director of the National Economic Council
records.about: A May 11, 2026 Yahoo Finance article. The byline and page metadata date it May 11, 2026. This page uses it only for the office. The October 2 transcript does not state one.
records.capture_status: pinned before the registry rule of 2026-09-08; fetch route not recorded

records.title: White House top economist doesn't expect more rate hikes this year after September jobs miss
records.quote: According to Phelan's calculations, the economy needs to add only about 40,000 jobs per month to keep the unemployment rate at its current level.
records.about: Yahoo Finance's interview with Chris Phelan, chair of the President's Council of Economic Advisers, including his calculation of about 40,000 jobs a month.

records.title: Federal government employment, monthly
records.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), from BLS
records.about: Federal government employment, in thousands, seasonally adjusted. Saved October 5. December 2024 is 3,009 thousand and September 2026 is 2,682 thousand.

records.title: Labor force growth, breakeven employment, and potential GDP growth
records.quote: Breakeven employment growth is the number of jobs that must be added to the economy each month to keep the unemployment rate steady while still absorbing the growth in the potential labor force.
records.about: The Federal Reserve note of April 2, 2026, defining break-even employment and estimating the pace at 155,000 in 2023-24, 85,000 in 2025, and less than 10,000 a month in 2026. The capture receipt's published date is not the date on the note.

records.title: Break-even employment declines as unauthorized immigration outflows continue
records.quote: net unauthorized immigration plummeted after early 2024
records.about: The Dallas Fed's March 31, 2026 note dating the decline in net unauthorized immigration to after early 2024, with net outflows beginning in February 2025.

records.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook
records.quote: close to zero net job creation over 2025 indicates a weak, and fragile job market
records.about: Governor Christopher J. Waller's February 23, 2026 speech. The page uses his sentence that close to zero net job creation over 2025 indicates a weak, and fragile job market.

records.title: Speech by Vice Chair Jefferson on the U.S. economy and monetary policy
records.quote: I see economic activity and labor market conditions remaining broadly solid while inflation remains above our target.
records.about: Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson's October 1, 2026 speech. He said he supported last month's increase, and that activity and the labor market remain broadly solid while inflation is above target.

records.title: Total nonfarm hires and separations rates, seasonally adjusted
records.about: The bureau's chart of hires and separations rates. The page states no publication date. Saved October 6, 2026. August hires rates are 4.2 percent in 2022, 3.3 percent in 2024, and 3.3 percent in 2026.

needs_ledger.plain: The committee raised the target range by a quarter point on September 16.
The 2026 calendar lists October 27-28 after the September meeting.
The August price index increased 3.4 percent from a year earlier.
August hires changed little at 5.2 million. The September release is scheduled for November 3.
The St. Louis Fed note puts the rate at 4.141 percent in August and 4.175 percent in September.

needs_ledger.need: September gain against the Reuters survey range
needs_ledger.plain: The preview's range runs from 35,000 to 180,000. September's 29,000 is below that low.
Job losers and job leavers fell. Reentrants and new entrants rose. The summary table is in the September release.
Table A-9 prints 8,986 in thousands. The facts view now says 8,986,000 people.

needs_ledger.need: Yearly wage gain as the Associated Press stated it
needs_ledger.plain: The Associated Press called the 3 percent yearly gain the smallest since May 2021. That sentence is in the facts view.

needs_ledger.need: Midterm setting in the Associated Press dispatch
needs_ledger.plain: The dispatch places the report a month before midterm elections. That sentence is in the facts view, not a new section.

needs_ledger.need: Prediction markets, named reactions, the post-release market close, and a cause of the 29,000
needs_ledger.plain: The reader model has no section for reactions or for a market close, and the September employment release states no cause. Those items were not admitted into the story.

sources_admitted.evidence: The September release and the earlier pins, plus the September 16 policy statement, the FOMC calendar, the August personal-income release, the August hiring release, the ADP count, and the St. Louis Fed rate note.

derived_numbers_computed.evidence: Monthly changes, the 45,250 prior-twelve average, the 68,000 average for 2026, and the 3.02 percent wage change are arithmetic on the October 3 series files.

outlet_claims_verified.evidence: CNBC's 34.6-hour workweek is not in the release, which says 34.4 hours. The 29,000 gain and the 4.2 percent rate match the release.

section_grammar.evidence: The page sections follow the reader model: What happened, The catch, Where this sits, What we do not know yet, and The records. What happened next is absent.

chip_vocabulary.evidence: The graded outlet lines use the checked chip. CNBC's 34.6-hour workweek is not the release's 34.4 hours.

live_elements_guarded.evidence: The page has no live element. The chart reads the pinned payroll file.
